edges.effect_quant: Across randomized evidence, metformin improves ovulation compared with placebo and can improve ovulation when added to clomiphene in selected PCOS populations. A 2019 Cochrane review found higher ovulation rates versus placebo (OR 2.64, 95% CI 1.85 to 3.75) and higher ovulation rates for metformin plus clomiphene versus clomiphene alone (OR 1.65, 95% CI 1.35 to 2.03).
edges.population: women with polycystic ovary syndrome and oligo-ovulation or anovulatory infertility, especially those with insulin resistance or obesity
edges.mechanism: Metformin lowers hepatic glucose output and improves insulin sensitivity, which can reduce compensatory hyperinsulinemia and downstream ovarian androgen excess. That metabolic shift can help restore follicular maturation and ovulation in some women with PCOS.
edges.summary: The protective effect is real but not universal. Metformin tends to work better as an adjunct or in selected metabolic phenotypes than as a magic standalone fertility drug, which is why pooled reproductive evidence is positive overall but individual trials can look neutral depending on comparator and patient subgroup.
edges.caveats: The ovulatory benefit is heterogeneous by body mass index, comparator, and treatment context. In particular, some clomiphene-combination trials found little added value, so this edge should be read as a probabilistic fertility aid rather than a guaranteed ovulation inducer.

evidence.citation: SharpeA et al 2019 Cochrane Database Syst Rev
evidence.notes: Metformin for ovulation induction (excluding gonadotrophins) in women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
